title: Find Median From Data Stream
description:
Maintain the median while numbers are appended to a stream.

Implement the MedianFinder class:

  • __init__() creates an empty stream.
  • addNum(num: int) -> None appends one occurrence of num.
  • findMedian() -> float returns the median of all values added so far.

For an odd number of entries the median is the middle sorted value, returned as a Python float. For an even number it is the arithmetic mean of the two middle sorted values, also returned as a Python float (for example 2.0 or 2.5). In the displayed JSON output, integral floats appear without a decimal suffix (2.0 appears as 2). findMedian is called only after at least one addNum.

You are graded on a recorded sequence of calls on one live object. The first call names the class and passes constructor arguments; subsequent calls name methods and their arguments. The constructor and methods returning nothing report null; the result array has one entry per call.

Constraints:

  • -100000 <= num <= 100000.
  • At most 50000 calls.
  • Insertion should take O(log n) time and median lookup O(1).

Example 1:

Calls: ["MedianFinder","addNum","addNum","findMedian","addNum","findMedian"]
Arguments: [[],[1],[2],[],[3],[]]
Output: [null,null,null,1.5,null,2]

The middle of 1 and 2 averages to 1.5; adding 3 gives a median of 2.0.

Example 2:

Calls: ["MedianFinder","addNum","findMedian","addNum","findMedian"]
Arguments: [[],[-1],[],[-2],[]]
Output: [null,null,-1,null,-1.5]

A singleton has median -1.0, and the mean of -2 and -1 is -1.5.

Example 3:

Calls: ["MedianFinder","addNum","addNum","addNum","findMedian","addNum","findMedian"]
Arguments: [[],[5],[1],[9],[],[0],[]]
Output: [null,null,null,null,5,null,3]

Sorted values 1, 5, 9 give 5.0; after adding 0 the middle pair 1 and 5 gives 3.0.
